messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Nimble package running too slow
parts:
Dear Suzy,

I took a relatively brief look at your code.  It looks like you have 526*526 data points.  You have 526 multivariate normals, each of length 526, so each with a covariance matrix that is 526x526.  You are setting each of the covariance matrices to a diagonal matrix, so all covariances are 0.  Using dmnorm like this will force a costly matrix computation (including a Cholesky decomposition followed by a matrix multiplication or a solve) for every MCMC update of every parameter (and you have 12*526 coefficients).  If this is a toy working towards a case where you need non-zero covariances, then the answer might simply be that these are indeed costly computations for a large model.  But if this is really what you want, it would be better to use univariate normals and avoid the costly matrix computations.  Also, I'm not immediately following your model.  I've more often seen something like psi_y[i] * exp(-Dist[1:N, 1:N]/lambda) to calculate a covariance matrix.  You are using diag(psi_y[i] * exp(-Dist[1:N, i]/lambda)) to calculate each of i separate precision matrices.  Again, I might not be seeing it.  Often people provide some explanation of their model when posting to this list.  If you need greater clarity on what your model code is creating, I'd suggest not using nimbleMCMC and instead building the model yourself using nimbleModel and exploring its calculations using model$calculate etc.  HTH.

Perry
